checks.description: Full active history blocks new-ID baseline; reviewed rollover/reconnect then separately reviewed new image job executes once, no maintenance image side effects.
Retry identity, full receipts and unknown dispositions preserved across archive/migration; invalid/corrupt/unsafe/duplicate history refuses.
Actual process contention and durable publication failure matrix preserve old/new complete view or refusal, never lose/replay identity; bounded orphan handling.
Live/unresolved work blocks maintenance; observed/disposed unknown outcomes remain truthful and never execute archived work.
Approved finite count/storage/inode/temporary ceilings, configured shared-data reserve and total-capacity refusal measured; no artifact deletion.
Actual maintenance review/apply/cancel/reconnect journey, archived pending-ID recovery, responsive reads and matched strict helper/UI staging with explicit evidence levels.
Relevant admin/jobs/resolution/transaction/staging regressions and source/JSON/Markdown/gitlink consistency, existing image safety/preservation and packaging/export paths intact.

constraints.text: Complete required G4 rollover, not a larger LIMIT or acknowledgement-only substitute. Demonstrate the full-128 baseline including one disposed unknown, browser observation/review/cancel without maintenance publication, explicit apply, disconnect/reconnect, and a separately reviewed safe-source image.cancel executing once afterward. Preserve every original receipt and unknown disposition and assert no maintenance backend install/mark/reconcile/reboot/health/slot/state mutation. Only a complete settled active batch may roll over; terminal or explicitly disposed unknown is eligible, while any queued/running/unresolved receipt blocks. Do not infer settlement merely from elapsed time, changed boot, absent worker or service inactivity. Existing resolution/service evidence remains at its original source revision; retain all original transaction/idle/customization/pinning/profile/heater/recovery gates.

Use one validated authoritative committed view for lookup across active plus all archives, before capacity, state, current-service or new-operation admission. Preserve all original plan fields, ID, boot, phase, message, queued time and complete bounded disposition evidence canonically or byte-for-byte. Same-ID/same-full-plan retries return historical outcome without execution; changed plans refuse at every capacity. Identical disposition acknowledgement retries return original retained disposition even after rollover/boot/state/service changes; changed disposition evidence refuses. Archived unknowns always render unknown, never succeeded/refused or retryable. Worker selection and result saving operate on active records only, preserve archive references, and reject an explicitly named archived/disposed ID before controller/backend construction or invocation. Test a delayed named old unit while a new active job is queued so it cannot consume that new job.

Before enabling writes, specify exact versioned manifest/object schemas, generation/revision binding and publication/recovery state machine. jobs.json is the sole commit point; validate the whole manifest and every referenced snapshot before any lookup or admission: supported version, strict fields/types, bounded names/lengths/counts/hashes, global unique IDs, receipt/disposition schemas, private ownership/modes, regular single-link no-symlink files and safe directory-relative access. The sole single-link exception is the migrated persistent ledger lock: ledger.lock and history-format-v2.lock must be exactly the two expected directory-relative names for the same held regular inode/device, with link count exactly two, administrator ownership, file mode exactly 0600 and private directory mode exactly 0700. Validate the held descriptor and both bound names after acquiring exclusion; reject missing, substituted, additional, symlinked, differently owned or differently permissioned aliases. Other locks, manifests, snapshots, receipts and temporaries retain single-link rules. Never treat missing manifest plus fence or history objects, missing referenced object, duplicate IDs, corrupt/unsupported format or invalid permissions as fresh empty history. Version two with a missing/damaged fence refuses. Refuse rather than reconstruct identity from orphan files. Define legal empty active snapshots and final-capacity manifests. Valid legacy lists remain observation-readable, with explicit reviewed migration retaining all complete rows; invalid or over-bound legacy input refuses without rewriting it. A valid fenced legacy state is an interrupted migration state, requiring explicit reviewed resume against its current complete revision. Do not automatically migrate on polling or retry.

Exercise real process contention plus injected interruption/error at object create/write/flush/file-fsync/no-replace publication/directory-fsync, manifest temporary write/file-fsync/replace/directory-fsync, parent-directory durability, cleanup and lost acknowledgement; include legacy migration and every subsequent active receipt/disposition/result save, not just rollover. Objects must be durable before the manifest commits; no worker launch or successful acknowledgement precedes durable receipt commit. A failed manifest durability acknowledgement after rename is unknown: reread the authoritative view, preserve both possibly required sets and never replay or destructively restore a stale manifest. At each boundary readers see a complete old/new committed view or truthful refusal, never a partial view or forgotten previously durable identity. Serialize writers under persistent lock inodes; document compatible lock ordering with worker->state->RAUC-writer->ledger and upload ledger->nonblocking-state->upload. Keep ledger exclusion short, never across service/transaction/device waits. Reclaim only proved uncommitted owned objects under exclusion after validating the committed view; never clean referenced history or guess through corruption. Repeated failures and restart must not accumulate unbounded orphans or require deletion of receipts to proceed.

Approve these finite engineering ceilings only: active 128; at most eight immutable full archive batches; at most 1152 distinct IDs; 67108864 allocated bytes total; at most sixteen batch-sized durable/temporary objects each <=2752512 encoded bytes with original receipt and disposition limits preserved; <=1048576 aggregate manifest/pointer/lock/directory metadata bytes; <=64 namespace entries/inodes. Account for current, candidate, previous possibly committed views, legacy source, all publication temporaries, directories, lock files and retained orphans at peak, not only steady state. Independently measure actual encoding, st_blocks, filesystem block rounding, metadata/inodes, memory/read cost and installed-byte delta at final implementation. The coordinator measurement is conservative ext4 allocation feasibility, not production or complete factory 8 GB fit. At total ceiling refuse new IDs and further rollover without offering eviction; identical retries, existing dispositions and observation remain usable within budget. A different ceiling or protocol changing reviewed scope needs an amended bounded review; destructive retention requires owner authority.

Implement concrete shared-/data admission for migration, maintenance and ordinary snapshot saves: account for peak incremental allocations and inode demand while preserving configured state/staging reserves (Store defaults 512 MiB with 256 MiB copy allowance; Staging defaults 768 MiB reserve and 130-inode admission), including existing uploads and other persistent data. Reserve is not archive allowance. Identify supported concurrent allocators and exclusion/recheck or reservation behavior; preflight is not a quota guarantee against unrelated privileged writers. Exercise concurrent upload/state-copy/history allocations, exact reserve and inode edges, ENOSPC during every publication stage and repeated failure. Refuse before starting new work if durable admission/result storage cannot be supported; preserve original manifests, receipts, images, uploads, user data and diagnostic evidence. Do not consume or lower accepted copy/upload reserve to make 64 MiB fit. Leave final factory-artifact and physical-power-loss gates open unless separately measured.

Trace and preserve all Jobs.load consumers and artifact dependencies across archives, specifically runtime/sv08_admin_upload.py Uploads.view/referenced/admitted/cleanup: nonterminal unknown receipts currently block uploads and historical stage plans protect bundles when the journal is missing or mismatched. Do not hide archived unknown/terminal rows from these checks, replace raw phase rules with disposition eligibility, or permit artifact deletion merely because a receipt was archived. The supplied ownership list omits this file; coordinator must reconcile narrowly required upload integration/test ownership before implementation. Separate active writable snapshots from authoritative all-history lookup so combined rows are never saved as one 128-row active ledger. Test archived stage dependencies, missing/failed/mismatched journal, cleanup review invalidation and disposed-unknown preservation. Keep accepted upload behavior; changing artifact retention semantics is outside this approval.

Deliver reachable browser maintenance status/review/apply/cancel controls through strict fixed privileged RPC with no caller-supplied paths/executables. Bind review to complete committed-history revision and exact eligible identities; stale review refuses under lock. Maintain truthful active/archive/total remaining capacity and distinct reasons for unresolved work, no-space and final ceiling. Reconnect must recover a locally pending submission ID from archives without generating a new ID or automatically resubmitting; explicit identical retry remains supported. Include lost maintenance acknowledgement/idempotent completion recognition, concurrent/stale review, authentication-authority changes, no-space/corrupt history diagnostics, unchanged unsaved drafts, and responsive initial/polling history before state reads while a real separate worker holds a transaction barrier. Render unknown dispositions truthfully and ensure maintenance plan kinds cannot fall through image.submit or ordinary apply. Use real browser plus separate worker/backend fixture; label browser shim, actual authenticated Cockpit/helper and actual service supervision distinctly. Reuse unchanged authenticated/service evidence only with its exact revision and demonstrate matching current installed helper/UI/worker wiring; no shim claim becomes authenticated evidence.

Prove complete preservation/export/update compatibility paths, not just active helper edits. Stage matching runtime/UI/worker and hash inventory through scripts/integrate_host_os.py, scripts/stage_admin_ui.py and recovery assembly scripts/recovery_image.py as applicable. The existing recovery export inventories its whole quiescent source; test that exported bytes include manifest and every referenced active/archive snapshot, original unknown evidence and legacy history and can be inspected as one validated committed view; source-change/export failure must not publish a misleading complete archive. Cover read-only source and destination bounds; export never licenses history deletion. Shared history survives A/B rollback, update and restore without generation-copy rollback or flattening. Replace only the earlier universal old-reader guarantee with this exact boundary: unchanged bare internal load() returns [] for an absent jobs.json, and internal load/save bypasses are not supported admission. Newly admitted unchanged old public history, submit, disposition and upload ledger paths, and the named worker, must refuse the intact paired fence without history mutation for present versioned, absent, malformed and valid-list-replaced manifests. Trace each supported entrypoint, including old-slot and later correctly signed old-runtime routes, to the actual fenced lock; do not infer coverage from one history() probe or matching-runtime staging. Pre-admitted old waiters are governed by the separate contention constraint, not retroactive lock validation. Arbitrary privileged deletion/replacement of compatibility metadata and authoritative history is outside the supported protocol; do not claim tamper containment or safety from corruption of both fence and manifest. New supported writers must refuse missing/corrupt committed history and damaged version-two fences before new identity admission. Old-slot boot and rollback remain available; old history mutation refusal must not become a new boot, health or signed-policy restriction. Do not silently change accepted signed metadata or health/recovery policy; coordinator reconciles necessary integration ownership or records an exact blocker before claiming completion.

Delivery requires fresh independent feature_verifier_high review of the complete candidate and all seven named acceptance checks, including deterministic offline crash/concurrency evidence and full browser journey. The approver, planner, author and evidence-producing implementation/integration sessions are not that verifier. Run affected jobs/resolution/upload/admin/transaction/staging/export/compatibility regressions, JSON/Markdown/diff/indexed-gitlink/lock consistency checks and record dated source-bound evidence with explicit offline levels. Fix the proposal reference to absent accompanying plan.md in coordinator records or supply its equivalent exact ownership/task handoff; inline ownership is the reviewed boundary. No new dependency, daemon, scheduler, external spending, hardware operation, network/credential access, release decision or retention destruction is granted; original candidates and historical identities/evidence remain preserved.

Fence creation is permitted only in explicit reviewed migration/apply after excluding active workers under worker then ledger and any required higher-lock order. Create the exact alias using held directory-relative access, never unlink/replace/rotate ledger.lock or introduce a second exclusion inode. Establish file/directory and required parent durability for the validated pair before publishing any archive or version-two manifest. Inject failure before/after link creation, alias validation and each durability boundary, as well as every manifest publication boundary. Fence-before-manifest interruption retains a valid legacy committed view and a monotonic fence; observation may read it and explicit resume must revalidate its current revision. Do not remove a fence after uncertain publication or restore stale legacy bytes. Use actual old/new processes and barriers to admit an unchanged old waiter through its pre-flock validation before fence creation: after successful version-two publication it must refuse without save/backend invocation; after pre-manifest interruption it may access current legacy data under the same inode, so preserve its durable changes and prove new resume never publishes a stale prepared snapshot. If that old process precedes the migrator, migration must likewise revalidate after acquiring exclusion. Test submit's two ledger acquisitions, disposition's repeated acquisitions and delayed named workers. No supported operation may unlink jobs.json; demonstrate atomic replacement leaves no missing-manifest publication window. Preserve the distinction between supported publication crashes and external manifest deletion during a pre-admitted old process, which this unchanged code cannot contain. The old executable constructs installed context before Jobs.work; do not claim blanket refusal before controller construction.

Reconcile narrow runtime/sv08_export.py and associated export/readback/history-test ownership before implementation. Current generic export serializes the aliases independently and cannot be counted as relationship-preserving. Deliver an explicit bounded representation of the exact validated ledger.lock/history-format-v2.lock relationship, bound to the exported committed history and verified by semantic readback; reject unexpected link relationships and preserve existing archive path, duplicate-member, sparse-expansion, destination-bound, checksum and no-replace publication protections. Source validation must work read-only without creating or repairing source locks. Include link count and both aliases' held inode relationship in source-stability validation, so alias removal/addition/replacement cannot pass as an unchanged source. In an isolated restore fixture demonstrate the exact two names become one owned 0600 regular inode with nlink two in a 0700 private directory, with durable complete history, before enabling writes or exposing it to an old helper. Restore must have exclusion from live helpers/workers and open lock waiters; never replace a live exclusion inode. A relationship-aware reconstruction is allowed only in an explicitly reviewed restore path, not observation or ordinary startup repair. Missing manifest, missing alias, copied independent lock files, extra links, corrupt history and interrupted restoration must refuse write admission. Where no supported restore integration exists, prove the destination is refused before enabling writes and retain that exact limitation; do not invent a general restoration service or claim round-trip acceptance. OS restore/update/A/B rollback must preserve the existing shared history in place. Exported bytes alone, or new-code refusal while an old helper remains able to write flattened history, does not satisfy this constraint.

The planner's common persistent private allocation.lock is accepted as a leaf-lock refinement, retaining single-link validation and existing lock orders. It may acquire no higher lock. Integrate all claimed supported allocators: history publication, Uploads streaming, Staging.receive/receive_locked including direct callers, and Store generation creation/copy. History uses ledger->nonblocking allocation; upload uses ledger->nonblocking state->upload->nonblocking allocation and releases higher locks before streaming without reacquisition; state copy uses state->allocation. Hold allocation only through bounded allocation/publication/cleanup, never service/backend/device waits. Preserve a common configured byte floor F=max(Store.reserve_bytes+Store.copy_limit_bytes, Staging.reserve_bytes), plus separately reserved future publication headroom H of at least two maximum batch allocations and the full metadata allowance rounded to filesystem blocks, with 64 future history inodes. New admissions preserve F plus worst incremental peak plus H; result/unknown/disposition publication may use H while preserving F and its actual peak, with no new identity until headroom is restored. H is free-space admission, not additional stored history or an increased ceiling. Preserve existing Store copy-size/free-space/inode tests and Staging allocated-upload plus configured reserve/130-inode tests, adding rather than replacing the stronger common floor/headroom checks. Include lock/directory creation and configured nondefault reserves, avoid double-counting existing allocated data, and explicitly name uncooperative allocators outside this protocol. Prove exact byte/inode edges, process contention, busy refusal, result-publication failure without replay, and bounded debris recovery. No claim of filesystem quota, throughput improvement or full factory fit follows from this design.

decision.rationale: Approved only the bounded technical amendment at source 944128e5faaca63a7157ad83b4256d3c2a74923a. ADR 0010 and the actual jobs/resolution requirements require retained disconnect-surviving history and the usable full-capacity rollover journey; this amendment changes neither those owner requirements nor numeric ceilings. Before: old Jobs.load returns [] when jobs.json is missing, and a new-only format marker cannot change that. After the proposed durable fence: newly admitted unchanged old public history/submit/resolution/upload/worker paths encounter Jobs.lock's existing st_nlink != 1 rejection. Source runtime/sv08_admin_jobs.py validates the opened inode before flock; preserving that inode therefore preserves exclusion but does not retroactively reject pre-admitted waiters. Those waiters must be tested separately: complete versioned publication makes old load refuse; a fence-before-manifest crash leaves authoritative legacy data, which an already admitted old waiter can still access under the same exclusion. New code must reread that legacy view before explicitly resuming migration. No supported publication may unlink the authoritative manifest. The supplied compatibility/fence-probe.json supports same-inode retention, link count two and old public history refusal with an absent manifest, while explicitly preserving bare load's empty result; it does not prove concurrency or export/restore. Concrete integration gap: runtime/sv08_export.py member() emits both source names as independent regular members, identity() omits link count, and verify_stream() rejects hardlink members. Current export therefore does not preserve the fence relationship merely by inventorying both names. Narrow relationship-aware export/readback integration and explicit restore validation or refusal are required below; generic flattening is not accepted. Shared allocation exclusion and future result headroom are compatible refinements of accepted reserve requirements, subject to exact-edge and concurrency evidence. RAUC signed policy and matching-runtime staging alone do not gate every unchanged old helper; the persistent fence supplies the proposed supported-public-entrypoint gate without new signed metadata, boot-health masking or loss of A/B rollback. All original constraints are carried forward, with only the paired-ledger single-link exception and precise old-public-entrypoint contract replaced. Evidence level: source-only review, with supplied source-only feasibility observation; no reviewer experimental probes, delivery tests, installed acceptance, hardware or release evidence. Actual proposal/requirement bytes were independently SHA-256 hashed and match context.json; feature_workflow.py review-context independently returned the scope binding below. The preserved archive is docs/features/host-image-history-rollover/approval-20261001.json; the requested archivedapproval-20261001.json filename does not exist. This is a separate session from the planner/author. Requested fallback is GPT-6.1 Sol/medium; inspected session output identifies this thread but provides no independently observable effective model/effort, so the coordinator must verify launch settings before relying on the review tier.
